why: A convergence hub is a place where several lines' own digitised geometry — or, more often, several FOLLOWERS of one canonical part — sit inside one small radius of a shared terminal or junction throat. The general lane pass ranks lanes by measured lateral offset over a window at least MIN_RUN_METRES long, then may flatten a whole display class onto its busiest lane (DOMINANT_LANE_SHARE). Both rules are right for a normal corridor and both are wrong inside a hub: the convergence itself is shorter than MIN_RUN_METRES by construction (that is what makes it a throat rather than a corridor), and a hub routinely bundles several lines of the SAME display class (same operator/colour) that the general pass never even compares to each other, because same-class parts are deliberately excluded from being neighbours (see displayClassKey / the neighbour scan in build-display-lanes.mjs) — that exclusion exists so one line's own repeated geometry never fights itself for a lane, but it also means two DIFFERENT branches of one operator that happen to converge on the same platform throat never get measured against one another at all, and both default to lane 0.

The hub pass in build-display-lanes.mjs runs after the general pass and only touches rows inside a hub radius: for every canonical part crossing the radius, it collects that part plus every part (of any display class) whose OWN geometry also passes inside the radius, orders them by branch-block (which side each one's geometry departs to beyond the hub, left before continue before right), and assigns evenly spaced half-integer slots centred on zero — the same i-(n-1)/2 scheme rail-stroke.js already ramps smoothly to and from.

The 17 Japanese hubs added 2026-09-04 name the throats where the Japan audit found several operators' own digitised geometry inside one small radius. Three of them (新宿, 池袋, 札幌) deliberately declare NO trunkLineId: at 新宿 and 池袋 no single railway owns the alignment the others converge on — the JR lines, the 私鉄 termini and the subways each approach on their own structure — and at 札幌 the convergence is one JR line meeting two subways that cross it underground. Left without a trunk, computeHubOverrides picks the member the most follow rows name as canonical, which is the right default exactly when no railway can be said to own the place.
